Krusader 2.4.0 makes Shift plus a function key work in the web desktop, finally closes the pasted-uppercase bug for real, and gives the container start a readable banner.

## ✨ Added

- **A readable init banner.** The startup log opens with a knight ASCII banner and a one-line title, instead of the previous multi-line block that competed with the base image's own branding.
- **The READY line carries its own colour.** Green when the web UI came up, red when it did not, so a failed start is visible at a glance in the Unraid log view.

## ⚡ Improved

- **`UMASK` now defaults to `000`.** At `022` every file Krusader created landed at 644, which no other container running under a different user ID could write. On a shared Unraid folder that is a dead end you only notice much later.
- **The build pins what it pulls.** GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and the container base images to digests, so a rebuild cannot silently pick up a different upstream.
- **One support section everywhere.** The README, the app's About card and the Sponsor menu now say the same thing, and the Unraid support thread is linked where people look for it.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Shift plus a function key lost its Shift.** Shift+F4 arrived as a bare F4, so Krusader opened the editor instead of the New Text File dialog, and on a folder it only answered that folders cannot be edited. Shift+F2 and the other such shortcuts behaved the same way.
- **Why that happened.** The web desktop's key injector lifts a held Shift around a keystroke when the key's level does not want it. That is right for letters and wrong for a function key, since F4 carries the same symbol with and without Shift. The image now keeps the Shift on keys Shift does not change, and drops the patch once the base image ships the upstream fix.
- **Pasted UPPERCASE text keeps its case, this time for good.** The earlier attempt was reported as fixed but was not: the base image did not actually carry the upstream keyboard fix, and issue #27 came back. The image now builds on a base that genuinely contains it, so text copied in Firefox or Safari arrives unchanged.
